tess-rt: Pushed priority-scheduler + burst-adaptive-window to canary this morning. dropping the write here with numbers and rollout plan.
omar-rt: quick TL;DR please?
tess-rt: p50 flat, p95 -13%, p99 -24% on mixed bursty workloads for kernel-hotpath models. token cost down ~13% in canary.
vinay-bench: whoa 24% p99 is solid. where do gains come from?
tess-rt: two things: 1) priority-scheduler biases packer/coalescer to keep short-ready requests moving (reduces head-of-line blocking), 2) burst-adaptive-window smooths microburst packing so we avoid packing churn under spikes. together they reduce tail amplification.
zara-sre: any changes to error/retry behavior?
tess-rt: no increase in 5xx or retries. one transient where the adaptive window overshot during a synthetic stress test and triggered the short-circuit fallback, which kept user-facing errors at 0.
vinay-bench: bench command for reproducibility:```bash
./stress_bench --model kernel-hotpath --qps 1200 --burst 8x --seq-mix short:70,med:25,long:5 --dur 45m --scheduler priority --burst-window adaptive
```
tess-rt: summary numbers (canary vs baseline):
- baseline p99: 312ms -> canary p99: 237ms
- baseline p95: 128ms -> canary p95: 112ms
- baseline cost/token: $0.00059 -> canary: $0.00051
- sustained throughput at 95th +9% under burst
maya-pm: great — can we include one sentence for the product notes?
tess-rt: "Priority scheduler + burst-adaptive window reduce tail latency and lower inference cost for bursty real-time workloads."
zara-sre: rollout plan? health checks?
tess-rt: staged by region and capacity group: canary -> 25% groups for 1.5h -> 50% for 3h -> full. health checks: p99, 5xx rate, packer-thrash, backlog-queue-length, and fallback-trigger-rate. auto-rollback if p99 regresses >5% vs baseline over 10m or if 5xx rate increases >0.15% absolute.
zara-sre: adding dashboard tiles and alerts: packer.thrash > baseline+4% (5m), backlog.queue > baseline+50 (5m), gpu_mem.used > baseline+200MB (10m). also monitoring fallback-trigger-rate closely.
omar-rt: validated on fp16/int8/int4?
tess-rt: yes across fp16/int8; int4 validated on a reduced sample. no kernel changes required, just runtime ordering and packing heuristics.
vinay-bench: any perf cost on very small single-request latencies?
tess-rt: tiny p50 increase (~2ms) for extremely tiny sequences in non-bursty steady state; tradeoff was acceptable given p99 improvements. documented in PR #4622.
cto-luke: please add a short blurb for the next all-hands and note the cost improvements. great work.
tess-rt: drafting release note: "Reduced p99 latency by up to 24% and lowered per-token cost via priority scheduling and burst-adaptive packing. Rolling out gradually with conservative rollback thresholds."
deploy-bot: Canary deployment initiated for group: kernel-priority-canary. 25% -> running health checks.
zara-sre: early graphs look healthy at T+25m. no abnormal fallback spikes.
ovinay-bench: posting full bench graphs and config knobs in #eng-runtime after full rollout.
tess-rt: follow-up: I'll publish a short playbook on tuning the adaptive window and priority weights for different workload mixes.
cto-luke: awesome 389
vinay-bench: :thumbsup:
